text: Writing clean code is a crucial skill for any developer. At its heart, it means writing code that is easy for other people (and your future self) to read and understand. This starts with using clear naming conventions. For example, a variable called `userAge` is far more meaningful than `x`, and a function named `calculateTotalPrice` tells you exactly what it does. Instead of writing one long, confusing block of logic, you should break your program into small, focused functions, each with a single purpose. This approach greatly improves maintainability; when a bug appears, you can quickly find and fix it without having to decode the entire program. In the end, clean code saves time, reduces frustration, and makes collaboration much more enjoyable.
